text:
Jordan Greenway is the kind of player whose box score tells you almost nothing, which is lucky, because his box score is grim: one goal, one point in 16 games for Chicago, and nothing in the 15 games since. At 6'6" and 231 pounds, the former Wild and Sabres winger is there to kill penalties, finish checks (32 hits) and get the puck deep.

Some of the drought is bad luck. He has 2.41 expected goals (the quality of his chances, measured in goals) and one goal to show for it. But the chances have thinned lately, and his ice time has slipped to about 12 and a half minutes. At five on five, Chicago gets just 41% of the expected goals with him on the ice, slightly better than the team does without him.

Evolving-Hockey rated him around replacement level last season. He is 29 and carries a piece of history: in 2018 he became the first African-American named to a U.S. Olympic hockey roster. Can he give the Blackhawks a penalty kill they trust and the few goals his chances say he is owed? Our range has him finishing the season with 5 to 13.
headline: Jordan Greenway's job in Chicago isn't scoring
